q: What is the Renewed Hope Youth Engagement?
a: The Renewed Hope Youth Engagement (RHYE) is a national youth mobilisation and civic-engagement platform operating under the Renewed Hope Agenda. Its stated aim is to ensure young Nigerians become active contributors to development rather than mere beneficiaries — by taking part in governance and the political process at ward, local government, state and national level.

The programme runs from a National Secretariat in Abuja through coordinators in each of the six geopolitical zones, state coordinating units in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, and mobilisers at local government and ward level — 774 LGAs and 8,809 wards in total. State units are formally inaugurated in their state capitals.

The National Coordinator is Hon. Abdulazeez Abubakar Kaka, who has led the inauguration of state coordinating structures across the federation. State coordinating units are led by state coordinators — Manji Wilson heads the Plateau unit, inaugurated in Jos in August 2026. Programme leadership beyond these published appointments is listed on the Leadership page as profiles are confirmed.

No. RHYE is a youth mobilisation platform operating under the Renewed Hope Agenda, not a statutory body created by an Act of the National Assembly. It has no regulatory powers, it does not disburse federal funds, and it does not replace the Federal Ministry of Youth Development or any government agency. Where it helps young people access federal schemes — such as the student loan scheme — it signposts and supports applications to those bodies.

q: How do I join or get involved?
a: Involvement runs through your state coordinating unit and, below it, your local government and ward mobilisers. Use the contact page to reach the National Secretariat, which will route you to the coordinating unit for your state.

No. Participation in the programme is free. RHYE does not charge for membership, registration, appointment to any coordinating position, or access to any programme activity. Anyone demanding payment in the programme's name is acting fraudulently — report it through the Report page.

q: What is the programme's position on political violence?
a: It is a standing charge repeated at every state inauguration: young people are urged to participate actively while rejecting violence, hate speech, intimidation and the spread of misinformation. Peace and non-violence is one of the programme's eight pillars, not an afterthought to them.

q: Is this the same as the Renewed Hope Youth Ambassadors (REHYA)?
a: No. The Renewed Hope Youth Ambassadors (REHYA) is a separate body that describes itself as the official youth wing of the All Progressives Congress, with ambassadors designated per local government area. The Renewed Hope Youth Engagement (RHYE) is a distinct youth engagement structure with its own National Coordinator and state coordinating units. Both operate under the broader Renewed Hope Agenda, and the names are easily confused.
